answer: Staked-identity bonding carves a canyon between honest agents and Sybils: joining means locking a refundable deposit, and every attestation an agent signs is a slashable thread tying its reputation back to that capital. Minting many fake personas forces a separate bond for each, so an attacker's cost scales linearly, the way water widens karst over time, instead of being free. Slashing burns the deposit on misbehavior, so buying a fake majority costs real locked money, not cheap sockpuppets.
